answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the oasis check immediately, the thread audit keeps the resolved set and the ferrous replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 54 aliases as a result forfeits the reading cost 54 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 18 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
